title: Abstract Particle Art with Dragon Model
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive abstract particle art scene using Three.js. Load the 'DragonAttenuation.glb' model using GLTFLoader from a CDN.

## Scene Setup
- Black background (0x000000)
- PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 8), looking at origin
- Ambient light (0x222244, intensity 0.3) and a point light (0xffffff, intensity 1.5) at (5, 5, 5)
- Load 'DragonAttenuation.glb' model, center it at origin, scale it so its bounding box longest axis is approximately 3 units. Make the dragon semi-transparent (opacity 0.4) with a wireframe material overlay.

## Particle System
- Create a particle system with exactly 2000 particles using THREE.Points with THREE.BufferGeometry
- Particles start in a sphere of radius 5 around the origin, with random positions
- Each particle has attributes: position, velocity (initially zero), color (random HSL with saturation 0.8, lightness 0.6), and size (random 0.02-0.08)
- Particles should orbit around the dragon model with a gentle swirl force
- Use additive blending for the particle material with a small circular texture (generated via canvas)

## Particle Modes (cycle with 'M' key)
- Mode 0 'ORBIT': Particles orbit the dragon with a swirl force. Apply a gentle pull toward the dragon surface.
- Mode 1 'EXPLODE': Particles explode outward from center with random velocities (speed 2-5 units/s), then slowly decelerate (damping 0.98)
- Mode 2 'ATTRACT': Particles are strongly attracted to the dragon model center, creating a dense cluster. Attraction force = 3.0
- Mode 3 'WAVE': Particles arrange in a sine wave pattern along the X axis, y = 2*sin(x*0.5 + time), z = 2*cos(x*0.5 + time)

## Color Themes (cycle with 'C' key)
- Theme 0 'NEON': Hue cycles through full spectrum based on particle index
- Theme 1 'FIRE': Hue range 0-0.1, high saturation, warm colors
- Theme 2 'ICE': Hue range 0.5-0.7, cool blues and cyans
- Theme 3 'MONO': All particles white with varying brightness

## User Interactions
- Mouse click on canvas: Create a burst of 50 temporary particles at the clicked 3D position (raycasted onto a plane at z=0). These particles fade out over 2 seconds. Track total bursts in state.
- 'M' key: Cycle particle mode (0->1->2->3->0)
- 'C' key: Cycle color theme (0->1->2->3->0)
- 'R' key: Reset all particles to initial sphere positions, reset mode to 0, theme to 0
- 'Space' key: Toggle pause/resume of the animation
- Up/Down arrow keys: Increase/decrease particle size multiplier (range 0.5 to 3.0, step 0.25)
- Left/Right arrow keys: Increase/decrease rotation speed of the dragon model (range 0.0 to 2.0, step 0.1). Dragon auto-rotates around Y axis.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left overlay div (id='hud') showing:
  - Current mode name
  - Current theme name
  - Particle count (main + burst)
  - Size multiplier
  - Dragon rotation speed
  - FPS counter
  - Paused status
- Style: white text, semi-transparent dark background, monospace font, padding 10px

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- modelLoaded: boolean (true once dragon GLB is loaded)
- particleCount: number (main particles, should be 2000)
- currentMode: number (0-3)
- currentModeName: string ('ORBIT','EXPLODE','ATTRACT','WAVE')
- currentTheme: number (0-3)
- currentThemeName: string ('NEON','FIRE','ICE','MONO')
- sizeMultiplier: number (default 1.0)
- dragonRotationSpeed: number (default 0.5)
- isPaused: boolean (default false)
- burstCount: number (total click bursts triggered, starts at 0)
- activeburstParticles: number (currently visible burst particles)
- elapsedTime: number (seconds since start, stops incrementing when paused)
- dragonOpacity: number (0.4)
- dragonScale: number (the uniform scale applied)
- cameraDistance: number (distance from camera to origin)

## Animation Loop
- Update particle positions based on current mode each frame
- Rotate dragon model around Y axis at dragonRotationSpeed rad/s
- Update burst particles (fade and remove expired ones)
- Update HUD text
- Update __3D_STATE__ every frame
physics_constraints: Particles must stay within a bounding sphere of radius 20. Damping in EXPLODE mode is 0.98 per frame. Attraction force in ATTRACT mode is 3.0. All positions must be NaN-free. Burst particles must fade linearly over 2 seconds.
